lines: Phew. Okay. Breathing again. Hello, blue.
Railing, my old friend. Hold me up a minute.
Cooling down. The jasmine is warming up. Smell that!
Somebody's bougainvillea is glowing purple. Even now!
Stretch the calves, watch the lights. Best part of the run.
My grandmother ran this promenade. Slower, and singing.
Heart still going. Pom pom pom. Lovely.
The lemon tree by the kiosk has one new lemon. I checked.
Phew! The sky went blue while I was busy panting.
Home, shower, tomatoes on toast. That is the whole plan.
Mum says geraniums like a chat. I tell mine about my laps.
Lean, breathe, look. Lean, breathe, look. Got it.
The oleander on the corner smells like Sunday.
Two laps done. Zero regrets. One very pink face.
A pot of lavender for the balcony. Maybe two!
Good evening, string lights! You came on just for me.
Dad taught me to run. He also taught me to stop for views.
Okay, legs. You did great. You may go home now.
My little brother says I run like a happy duck. Fair.
Shoes still warm. Air going cool. Perfect swap.
Those cypresses look painted on. Very straight. Very proud.
Tomorrow, the long way round. Past the rosemary hedge.
Catching my breath. It ran off without me.
Someone left a sprig of mint on the bench. A gift!
Hello, sea! Sorry, I was busy breathing. Hello properly.
My nan's rule: always stop and smell one flower per lap.
Lap one: jasmine. Lap two: orange blossom. I keep score.
Best seat in town is a railing after two laps.
The window boxes under the zinc roofs are all red tonight.
Going home past the fig tree. It always says goodnight.
Count to sixty, then walk. Fifty-nine. Okay, ninety.
Plan for later: socks off, feet up, peach in hand.
The air smells like warm stone and geraniums. Mmm.
Grandad grew tomatoes taller than me. I grow chives.
Tomorrow I will wave at Inès first. Before she laps me.
Look, the lamps are on and the sky is still blue. Both!
That bougainvillea has climbed one more window this week.
Cool metal under the hands. Little reward.
Saturday plan: market, peaches, a new pot for the thyme.
Smells like Mum's garden. Rosemary and evening.
My lamp shadow is long and very pleased with itself.
Every lap I pass the same palm. We are close now.
Water bottle: empty. Breath: arriving any minute now.
Later: call Mum, tell her about the purple flowers.
The café planters have new marigolds. Very cheerful.
Running is how I find the best smells in town.
My aunt dries lavender in her hallway. I want that.
Tomorrow, pancakes. Lemon and sugar. From my own lemon!
Henri's lemon tree is shining in the café lights.
Stretching against the railing like a proper athlete.
Grandma said blue hour is when flowers close their eyes.
The sea went silver and I nearly forgot to breathe.
Home is ten minutes. I will make it fifteen. Slow walk.
Jasmine by the steps. I stop every single time.
Legs say home. Eyes say five more minutes. Eyes win.
I named my basil Pierre. Pierre is doing very well.
The breeze is doing my cool-down for me. Merci!
After tea, Pierre gets a bigger pot. He has earned it.
My dad still times my laps from memory. Badly. Kindly.
Next run, the rose garden route. Twice, if it smells.
Oof. Lovely oof. The good kind.
The kiosk has a little pot of pansies. Who did that? Bravo.
Every evening I think: one more lap. Every evening: no.
My sister sends me flower photos. I send her sky photos.
Blue sky, gold lamps, pink me. A matching set.
On the way home I say hello to the hibiscus. It is polite.
Ran past a garden of sunflowers. They all turned to look.
Breathing in for four, out for four. Smells like figs.
Okay, heart. Slow down. Nothing to chase now.
Grandad always said: stretch, then supper. I still do.
The first star! Right over the church. Hello!
Someone on the hill is watering pots. Good evening, pots!
Hands on the railing, face to the breeze. Bliss.
I keep a lemon in my pocket on long runs. For luck.
Next week I try for three laps. Then pancakes. Big ones.
The lamps look like a necklace on the promenade.
The rosemary by the fountain smells best after dark.
Cooling down slowly. Like the stones. Like the sea.
Lucie is leaning on the railing too. Two leaners, one view.
My windowsill: basil, chives, one brave strawberry.
There it goes, the last bit of blue. Thank you, sky.
I will dream about that bougainvillea. Probably purple.
Home soon. My lemon tree waits up for me. It is loyal.
A sprig of jasmine for Grandma. She will hum all week.
Done running. Now officially admiring. Very good at this.
Morning, lemon tree! You smell better than my shoes!
Bougainvillea! Pink already! Who is up earlier than me?
Lap one. Jasmine on the left. Heaven on the right.
Hello, cypresses! Standing so tall! I am trying!
Somebody watered the geraniums. They are sparkling!
Pancakes with lemon today. From that very tree. Probably.
My grandmother ran in sandals. I am in proper shoes. Still slower.
Mum says hello to the sea. I am passing it on. Hello, sea!
Phew! The oleander is out! Pink, white, pink, white!
Palm tree, palm tree, lamp post, palm tree. Lovely rhythm.
Big plan for today. Breakfast. Then a second breakfast.
Tomorrow I try three laps. Maybe. We will see. Probably two.
The rosemary by the steps! I brushed it! Smells like Sunday!
Huff. Puff. Lavender. Huff. Puff. More lavender.
Every window box is awake. Red, red, red, yellow!
Dad taught me to wave at every runner. So: hello, nobody yet!
That lemon has doubled in size since Tuesday! Go, lemon!
Fig tree by the church wall. Three figs. I am counting them.
Sun's coming up behind the roofs. Zinc going gold!
I smell bread. My legs smell it too. They are speeding up.
Halfway! Or a third. Somewhere very pleasant, anyway.
The fountain is still asleep. Shh. Tiptoe running.
Good morning, café chairs! Stacked up like sleepy cats!
Little sister wants a postcard. I will pick one at the kiosk!
Who planted all these marigolds? I want to shake their hand!
Bougainvillea on a blue door. Best thing I have seen all week.
Breathe in, orange blossom. Breathe out, happiness.
I ran here as a kid on holidays. Same corner. Same sunshine.
Grandad called this light the good light. He was right.
Later: lemonade, book, balcony. In that order. Very strict.
Bonjour, string lights! Off for now. Rest well!
Phew. The steps. My old friend. My puffing friend.
A tiny snail on the path. Good morning, sir. After you.
The basil on that sill is huge! Somebody loves it a lot.
Pink sky, pink flowers, pink cheeks. A matching set!
Today I am going to pick lemons with my aunt. Big basket!
Tomorrow, the long way round. Past all the roses.
Every morning the palms do a little wave. I wave back.
One more lap and I can smell the jasmine twice!
Whoosh. That was me. Very slightly whooshing.
Look at the shutters, all blue and sleepy. Lovely!
Mum's tomato plants would adore this sun. Lucky sun!
The bakery door just opened. That is my finish line.
Second lap is the good lap. The flowers know me by now.
Cypress, cypress, cypress. Like a row of green candles!
Somebody left a watering can by the fountain. Thoughtful!
Petals on the path. Pink confetti. Just for runners.
My cousin would love this. I am sending her a sunrise later.
Plan for tonight. Sunset at the railing. Already booked.
Hello, hydrangeas! Big as hats! Blue as Tuesdays!
Every lap the sun climbs one more roof. Nearly there!
I run, the gulls glide. They have the easier job.
Sea breeze on the left side only. My left side is very happy.
Thyme between the cobbles! Smell it when you step!
Lovely. Lovely. Out of breath. Lovely.
Up the promenade, down the promenade, up again. Wheee.
The bougainvillea has reached the second window! Climbing!
Grandma kept a geranium on every step. This town would suit her.
After this, a shower. Then the market. Then peaches.
Someone is frying onions already. Good morning, someone!
Huff. Hi. Huff. Lovely day. Huff. Bye!
Oh! A sparrow in the lemon tree! Two! A whole family!
The stone is still cool. My feet say merci.
Dawn smells like wet leaves and croissants. Best perfume.
I promised my brother a photo of this corner. Click. Done!
Every planter is a different colour. Like a paint box!
The palm by the kiosk has a new leaf. Look at it unfold!
Shoes tied twice today. Learned that one from Dad.
Lap two! The roses have opened since lap one! Show-offs!
Gold on the roofs, green on the hill. What a postcard.
Oh, the honeysuckle! I nearly stopped. I nearly did.
The window boxes look freshly painted. With flowers!
My mother says morning runs make the whole day kind. True!
Later I am repotting my little olive. It has earned a bigger home.
My little nephew calls palms pineapple trees. I like it better.
The light on the bougainvillea. Like it is lit from inside.
Sunrise today is apricot. Yesterday was peach. Both delicious.
This afternoon, a long lunch. Tomorrow, a longer lunch.
I keep a pressed flower from this street in my diary. Every year.
Oof. The air smells green. Is that possible? It is here.
Planning a picnic for Sunday. Lemons, cheese, a big blanket.
Somebody's grandad is watering his balcony in pyjamas. Hero!
The church bell! Seven. Or six. One of the good numbers.
Morning is the shy part of the day. Everyone whispers.
Dewdrops on every petal. Free little diamonds!
My aunt says jasmine at dawn is a good omen. Lots of omens!
Breath back. Okay. Hello. What a morning, eh?
The lemon tree by the corner always gets my first smile.
Tonight I will call Mum and tell her about the roses.
Lavender in my nose, sun on my neck. Perfect.
That bench has a pot of geraniums beside it. Like a friend.
Pancakes are cooling at home. Well, they will be.
Tap the fountain rim. Every lap. It is the rule. My rule.
Lucky socks today. One stripe, one spot. Very lucky.
I high-five the third lamp post. It never high-fives back.
Forgot to start my stopwatch. Again. Lovely lap anyway!
Headband on. Now I am a serious athlete. Mostly.
I named every lamp post. That one is Gérard. Morning, Gérard!
My form is perfect. My pace is a gentle suggestion.
Racing a pigeon. The pigeon is walking. Still winning.
In my head I am in the Olympics. Crowd going wild!
Shoelace check at the kiosk corner. Always that corner.
One sip of water at the halfway bench. Tradition!
I hum the same tune every lap. Nobody knows it. Me neither.
Breathe in for three, out for three. I lose count at two.
Personal best today! Best mood, I mean. Not best time.
I wave at my own reflection in the café window. Hi, me!
Every morning I pretend the finish line is just ahead. It works!
My knees sing a little song on the steps. Duet with my lungs.
I run like a happy giraffe. My cousin said so. Fair.
Lap two, and my ponytail is doing all the work.
Touch the cypress, turn around. Very official turning point.
I sprint the last ten metres. For drama. Every time.
Stretching later. Stretching is a promise I mostly keep.
Banana before, croissant after. That is my training plan.
Look at me go! Gently! Steadily! Somewhat!
Wrist watch says go. My legs say in a moment, please.
I nod at every cat on every step. It is only polite.
Sweatband on the left wrist. The right wrist is jealous.
Same route every day. Still find a new cobble to love.
My running face is very serious. My heart is giggling.
Whistle at the corner. Just one note. Morning sorted.
I chose bright yellow shoes. The sun is wearing matching ones.
Good morning, bench seven! Sit later. Promise!
I say bonjour to the bakery door. It smells back.
Tiny hop over the drain grate. Every lap. Nailed it.
My water bottle has a sticker of a snail. Motivational.
Elbows in, chin up, smile on. The smile is the easy bit.
Slow and steady wins the race. Good thing there is no race.
Once I tried running backwards. Lovely view, wobbly legs.
Deep breath at the top of the steps. Then a second one. Then go.
My cap is on backwards. Faster that way. Scientifically.
Big arm swings! I look like a windmill on holiday.
I am the second fastest runner in town. Out of two.
Every lap I spot something yellow. Today: a door!
My shadow is very long at dawn. Very long legs. Lucky shadow.
Quick wave at the kiosk. Owner not in yet. Wave stays.
Small skip at the fountain. Joy got into my feet.
My legs and I made a deal. Two laps, then waffles.
I wear a watch I never read. It just likes the fresh air.
My mum says I run like a song. A slightly breathless one.
Kick the dew off the curb. Little sparkle. Every morning.
Hello, string lights. I am the first bulb on today.
I listen to the gulls instead of music. Better tunes.
I like the bit by the café. Downhill. My favourite bit.
Quick thumbs up to the church clock. Right on time, both of us.
My stride is short. My smile is long. Fair trade.
Puff, puff, bonjour. Puff, puff, bonjour.
I tell myself a joke at the halfway point. Still laughing.
My new shoes squeak. Like tiny cheering fans.
I practise my finish-line pose on the promenade. Ta-da!
Jogging, not running. Jogging is running with good manners.
Always the same first step. Left foot. Lucky foot.
Hair tie number three. The first two ran off. Clever them.
On lap two I am a poet. Huff, puff, sky, sea, toast.
Every morning: touch the palm bark for good luck. Rough!
I am not slow. I am giving the sunrise time to catch up.
Lap one is warm-up. Lap two is also warm-up. I am very warm.
The cobbles go clip-clop. I am a happy pony.
Ah. The bench. My second-favourite piece of furniture.
Breath back in three, two, one. Okay, four, five.
My knees say good morning. Very loudly. Good morning, knees.
Little stretch, big yawn. The yawn is my favourite stretch.
Toast, honey, tea. The reward ceremony begins.
I keep a little notebook of laps. All of it says two.
Every runner needs a cheerleader. Mine is the bakery smell.
Pancakes are my medal. Syrup is the ribbon.
I always forget my keys in the other pocket. Found them!
Shower, breakfast, a little dance in the kitchen. Same order.
I hum my lap tune in the shower too. Still no idea what it is.
Wonderful run. Wonderful legs. Wonderful wobbly legs.
Water first, then coffee, then a very happy sigh.
I feel like a sunrise myself. A slightly sweaty one.
Tomorrow I will wear the other lucky socks. Both stripes.
Running is my way of saying hello to the whole town.
Hands on hips, look at the view. Best part of the run.
Gérard the lamp post is turning off. Night shift over, Gérard.
Ten good breaths at the railing before home. Always ten.
Best part of a run? The minute after. This minute. Lovely.
I tell my plant about the run when I get home. It listens.
Grandad ran with a handkerchief. I have a sweatband. Same idea.
Evening lap! Phew! The tiles are still warm!
Hello, fountain! Same splash as this morning!
Lap one... going well... mostly downhill in spirit.
The clock says half past six. My legs say lovely.
Shutters going pink! Every single one! Huff!
Bonsoir, awnings! Bonsoir, café! Bonsoir, everyone!
Left foot, right foot, croissant later. Good plan.
The lemon tree waved at me. Or the wind did. Both.
Second wind! Oh. That was just the sea breeze.
Running past the kiosk. Smells like peaches. Nice!
Mum says I run like a happy duck. She is right.
The string lights are not on yet. I will beat them!
Golden hour! Golden legs! Well, pink legs!
Counting cypresses... one... two... lost count. Fine!
Nearly halfway. Or a third. Lovely either way.
The fountain sounds like applause. For me? Merci!
Inès lapped me. She said bravo. I said huff.
Blue shutters, green shutters, blue again. Pretty!
I am not slow. I am sightseeing at a jog.
Excuse me, pigeon! Thank you, pigeon!
Dad taught me to wave at every runner. I wave a lot.
Phew! The promenade gets longer at golden hour.
That awning is striped like my running socks!
Big breath. Sea air. Bit of rosé air too.
Odile says I glow. I think it is mostly sun.
Lap two! The best lap! The one with the view!
The church bell rang. I took it as a cheer.
Shadow says go faster. Shadow is very tall today.
Hop over the drain cover... and the next one. Ha!
The church clock hands are gold now. So am I!
I run for the view. And the pancakes. Mostly pancakes.
My sister would love this light. I will tell her.
Every window on the hill... shining... like coins!
A gull just jogged beside me. Well, waddled.
Marcel is laying tables. I smell bread. Keep going!
Run, breathe, smile. Run, breathe, smile. Huff.
These tiles are blue and white. Like little waves!
Bonsoir, Henri! No, I cannot stop! Lovely hat!
The palms are swaying. I am swaying. We match.
Halfway point: the fountain. Quick splash on the wrists.
Phew. My knees are humming. Happy hum, though.
Somebody is playing accordion! Running in three-four!
That geranium box is new. Bravo, whoever!
Oops, nearly ran into a sunbeam. Sorry, sunbeam!
Grandma said: always finish the lap. I always do.
My watch says lovely pace. I made that up.
The zinc roofs are going orange. Like toast!
Every step... gets me closer... to the railing!
Look! The fountain dolphin has a sunset hat on!
Shoes untied? No. Just checking. Onward!
I ran this with my brother once. He sat on the bench.
The café chairs are all facing the sea. Like fans!
Gold on every cobble. Running on treasure!
Biscuit barked hello. Two barks. That is a lot.
Up the little slope! The tiny one! Huff! Done!
That shutter has a heart cut in it. Never noticed!
Running into the light. Very dramatic. Very slow.
Someone at the kiosk gave me a thumbs-up. Best medal.
Lap two is one lap. Then the railing. Easy maths.
I always sprint past the bakery. Self-control.
Is that lavender? Smells like Grandma's drawers!
Ah, the long shadows. Everybody is a giraffe.
Hello, Lucie! Save me a sip of sunset! Huff!
Breathe in sea, breathe out thank you.
Mum's rule: smile at the halfway mark. Smiling!
Runner's high? I think it is just a lovely evening.
Phew! Leaving footprints of pure joy. Probably.
Every tile I step on is a good tile today.
Two laps. One town. Zero rush. Well, a bit of rush.
The church clock chimed half past. Right on time. Me too!
My cheeks are pink. The sky is pink. Teamwork!
I taught my nephew to jog. He sprints, then naps.
The terracotta pots are glowing! Like lanterns!
Huff... huff... is that the sea? Yes! Still there!
The cobbles go clip-clop. Am I a pony? Feels like it.
Water bottle, check. Big smile, check. Breath, pending.
Same lap every evening. Never the same light.
I run so I can sit down later and mean it.
My dad ran with a towel round his neck. Me too now.
Ran past the clock so often, it knows my name.
Is that the smell of grilled peppers? Keep running!
A slow lap is still a lap. A very scenic one.
Phew! Does anyone else see seven shades of orange?
Shutters closing like sleepy eyes. Not mine! Huff!
My shoelaces are yellow. Golden hour approved.
Every time I pass, someone waves. Every single time!
I promised my mum one photo of the sky. Taking ten.
Garlic and butter from the café. My nose says stop. Feet say no!
Somebody is frying onions. Best smell on the whole lap!
Huff! Tonight I am having ratatouille. A big bowl of it.
The fountain gurgles. My tummy gurgles back. Supper soon!
Fresh basil on a windowsill! I ran slower just to sniff it.
Clink, clink, glasses at the café. Sounds like a toast to me!
Thinking about a cold lemonade with mint. Two more streets!
My shoes squeak on the marble bit. Squeak, squeak, hello!
Rosemary bush by the steps. I brushed it. Now I smell lovely.
Someone's grilling sardines. Smells like every summer ever!
After this lap: soupe au pistou. Mum's recipe. Huff, huff!
Fig tree by the wall! The figs smell like jam already.
A spoon tinkling in a cup somewhere. Tiny bell. Keep going!
Fresh-cut grass and sea salt. The town's own perfume.
I can hear the café espresso machine hiss. Pfff! Same as me!
Tonight's plan: socca with too much pepper. Perfect.
The palm fronds rustle like paper bags of chips. Hungry now.
Orange blossom! Huff! Someone has a tree nearby!
Pétanque balls clacking by the square. Clack! Good shot!
My water bottle sloshes. Slosh, step, slosh, step. A song!
Thinking of a peach tart. Not a peach. A whole tart. Huff!
Thyme growing in the cracks. Each step smells like supper.
Lap two fuel: one apricot. It was very good. Very sticky.
Somebody is whistling in the kitchen. Same tune as my feet!
Warm baguette under someone's arm. I smelled it from far!
The tiles here are smooth as butter. Careful! Lovely though.
Sunscreen and salt and onions. That is golden hour, really.
Cicadas still going! They cheer louder than I run.
Pancakes are for morning. Tonight is grilled aubergine!
The awning flaps like a little drum. Thump, thump. Thank you!
My nana made fish soup every Friday. This street smells like it.
Hot cobbles under my soles. Like running on fresh bread.
Ice cubes rattling in a jug somewhere. Yes, please, later!
A tomato salad with olive oil. That is my finish line.
Huff! Smelled vanilla. Looked around. It was a candle shop!
Wet stone by the fountain smells like rain. Lovely, lovely.
Brushed past the jasmine. My sleeve will smell nice all week!
The string lights buzz a tiny bit. Like bees getting ready.
Somebody slicing melon on a balcony. I can hear it. Juicy!
Phew! My cheeks are warm as a fresh madeleine.
Olive oil and lemon on the air. Somebody is doing it right.
The bakery fan blows sugar smell right onto the street. Huff!
Chopping sounds from an open window. Tak, tak, tak. Supper!
Supper is cold cucumber soup. I earned it. Nearly.
The breeze tastes salty. Free seasoning for runners!
Footsteps echo under the arches. Sounds like a whole team!
Café smells like toasted almonds. I will run past twice.
Grilled corn somewhere! Smoky and sweet. Huff! Happy nose!
My sneakers go pat-pat on the boards. Like a gentle clap.
A shutter creaked open. Someone is airing out a kitchen. Yum!
Little girl eating a cherry ice. She waved with it. Sweet!
Pine smell from the hill. Sticky, warm, wonderful.
I can hear a wooden spoon on a pan. Clonk! Someone cooks well.
Chickpea salad waiting at home. In the fridge. Calling me.
Laundry on a line smells like soap and sunshine. Best lap ever!
Huff! Café is setting out olives in little dishes. Green ones!
The fountain splashes my shins. Cold! Thank you, fountain!
Smells like hot tarmac and honeysuckle. Weird. Wonderful.
Gravel, tiles, boards, cobbles. My feet get a full menu tonight.
Running and dreaming of tagliatelle. With lots of parmesan.
Someone opened a fizzy water. Pssht! Me next, after the lap!
Rhubarb crumble! I smell it! Somebody's grandma is home.
The railing is warm as a teapot. I tapped it. Lap two!
My Norwegian aunt sends brown cheese. Tonight, on toast.
Saw a waiter carry tiny pizzas. Plural! Running faster!
Basket of lemons on a step. Smelled like a fresh start.
Mint tea at the railing after. That is my whole plan.
A café cloth just snapped in the wind. Like a flag for me!
Smells of hot butter and sugar. Is someone making crêpes? Yes!
Ripe tomatoes on a stall. They smell like sun. Huff!
The quiet hum of an evening town. Fridges, chatter, gulls.
Grandpa's rule: run before supper, never after. Obeying!
Strawberries in a paper cone! A kid shared one. Merci!
Splash of the fountain, clack of a shutter. Town music!
Cool shade under the palms. Like a sip of water!
I hear sizzle. I smell garlic. I see the finish. Perfect.
Supper is grilled fish and new potatoes. Running for it!
Smells like toast near the bakery even this late. Magic.
My favourite part of the lap? The smell of the café door.
Socks soggy, heart toasty. A very good evening run.
Banana in one pocket. Keys in the other. Ready for anything.
I always end with a cold glass of milk. Like a big kid.
Somebody is cooking with saffron. The whole street is yellow.
The softest sound here is the fountain. I run to it each lap.
Ice lolly after the lap. Lemon, please. Always lemon.
Tonight I am making clafoutis. Cherries. Lots of cherries.
My legs creak like the café chairs. Friendly creak, though.
Takk, legs! Merci, lungs! Thank you, sea breeze!
Pocket full of almonds. Crunch, step, crunch, step.
The bread here is so good I run both laps for it.
Lap one! The shutters are opening as I pass. Applause!
Hello, fountain! Still splashing! Me too, sort of!
The clock says eight. My legs say much later.
Blue shutter, green shutter, blue shutter. Lovely rhythm.
Cat on the wall! Hello, cat! It did not move. Respect.
Left at the cypress. Right at the other cypress.
That awning is new. Striped! I approve, mid-stride!
Croissant smell, three o'clock. Must. Keep. Going.
Tile, tile, tile, crack I always skip, tile. Perfect.
The gulls have a lane too. They are not using it.
Good morning, palm tree! You look tall today!
Henri waved his watering can at me. I waved my whole self.
Halfway! Or a third. Round enough, anyway.
The fountain splashed my elbow. Free refreshment!
Every lap the café gets one more chair. Like magic.
Bonjour, bonjour, bonjour! Everyone gets one!
My shoelace came undone at the kiosk. Good spot for it.
Lap two. The town looks even nicer the second time.
A gull just jogged beside me. Well, waddled. Briefly.
Zinc roofs catching the sun. Shiny! I am also shiny.
Lucie rang her bell. I rang back. With my mouth. Ding!
I count windowboxes. Eleven geraniums so far!
Down the steps, mind the step, lovely steps.
Marcel is wiping tables in time with my feet.
If I slow down, it is to admire. Not to breathe. Mostly.
Fountain coins, fresh tiles, open shutters. Good report!
Inès lapped me again. She said hello both times!
Hello, string lights! Off for now. Sleep well!
Somebody painted that door yellow. Bravo, somebody!
The sea is on my left. Still there. Very reliable.
Morning, Biscuit! Morning, Yusuf! Biscuit first, obviously.
The awnings go up one by one. Like a slow wave.
Breathing in lemons. Breathing out happiness. Mostly air.
Fast past the bakery. Slow past the bakery window.
A pigeon gave way. Very polite pigeon.
Lap one done! Lap two, here I come, slightly slower!
The cobbles are counting with me. One, two, one, two.
I nodded at the cypress. It nodded back. Breeze, probably.
Watch out, Léo! Oh, he is faster than me. Carry on!
The fountain is my halfway flag. Hello, halfway!
Every shutter on that house is a different blue. Amazing!
Huff. That hill. Hello, view. Worth it. Huff.
My shadow is very long and very keen this morning.
Passed a tabby on a wall. Then it passed me. On the wall.
I wave at the clock tower every lap. It never waves back.
Lovely tiles. Terracotta. Warm. Like my face right now.
The sprinkler got me. Thank you, sprinkler!
Henri is watering the lemon tree. It is watering me.
Morning breeze from the sea. Free tailwind on this side!
Kiosk is open! Newspapers! Not now! After pancakes!
My feet go pat-pat. The fountain goes plish. A duet!
Odile said bravo. I will run on bravo for a week.
Turned the corner, smelled coffee, nearly turned back.
The promenade is long and lovely and I am on it!
Steady now. Shutter, awning, palm. Shutter, awning, palm.
A whole row of geraniums cheered. Silently. I heard it.
Last stretch! The bakery is a finish line, right?
Right foot, left foot, croissant. That is the order.

Puff! The clock struck as I passed. I take it personally.
Nobody is racing. I am winning anyway.
Morning, Théo! He raised his coffee. Like a medal!
I run past the same flowerpot twice. It grows on me.
Every bench is empty but one. Morning, Henri!
Feet: tired. Eyes: delighted. Mood: excellent.
Biscuit sniffed my shoe. Biscuit gives it a seven.
Seagull on the lamppost. Judge of the race. Fair judge.
Lavender by the steps. One deep breath. Back to it!
Waved at the kiosk. A newspaper waved back. Lovely.
Round the fountain twice for luck. Dizzy luck!
Hello, café chairs! You will see me soon! Sitting!
Phew! A lovely town to be out of breath in.
Hands on knees. Good morning, cobbles. Close up!
Laces retied. Biscuit supervised. Off again!
Breathing like a happy accordion. Hello!
Done! Well, nearly done. Done enough to say hello.
Shower, pancakes, then I sit and watch others run.

Just admiring that awning. And catching my breath. Both.
Sorry! Hello! Lovely morning! I am going that way!
A quick stretch by the fountain. The fish watched.
Pancakes are a reward. So is this view. Both, please.
The cat is still on the wall. I envy its warm-up.
My legs are wobbly but my smile is very steady.
Bit of shade under the palm. Ah. Ten out of ten.
I run so I can sit at the café with a clear conscience.
Tomorrow, same two laps. The town is always new.
Jasmine over that gate! I ran slower just to smell it.
Cups clinking on the terrace. Best metronome in town.

The palms are rustling like applause. Merci, palms!
Salt air, warm stone, fresh paint. What a breakfast for the nose.
Lovely hat, monsieur! Very sunny of you!
Rosemary hedge! I brushed it. Now my sleeve smells like lunch.

Orange blossom by the steps. One sniff per lap. House rule.
Washing on a line, flapping hello. Smells of soap and sun!

Bonne journée, Camille! Your scarf is the colour of apricots!
Morning, Théo! Good luck with whatever you are pretending to do!

Wet earth by Henri's pots. The whole corner smells of rain.

My shoes squeak on the wet tiles. Squeak, squeak, bonjour!
Gravel crunch under the palms. Like running on cereal.
Cool shade, warm patch, cool shade. The promenade is a stripy cat.

Welcome to town, visitor! The fountain is that way! Enjoy!
Mint in a window box. I did not pick it. I breathed it, though.

Morning, Léo's friend! Nice jump! Ten points!
The railing is warm already. The sun got up before me.
Sunscreen and sea breeze. Smells like summer, every lap.
Fresh bread somewhere and wind chimes somewhere else. Perfect.
The kiosk rack squeaks when it spins. A lovely little hello.
You have a lovely smile, neighbour! Thank you for the nod!
Cypress resin in the air. Like running through a pencil case.

Soft breeze, warm neck, cool knees. Excellent arrangement.

Gorgeous geranium, madame! You must talk to it every day!
Cicadas warming up. They tune. I jog. Orchestra soon.
Bonjour, monsieur! Your newspaper looks very good from here!
The zinc roofs ping as they warm up. Tiny morning bells.
Kind of you to step aside, monsieur! Merci! Lovely shoes!
Dew on the bench by the palms. Shiny, like a little lake.

Yusuf! Your walk is very relaxed. I admire it. From a distance.
Shutters smell of warm paint in the sun. Who knew?
The breeze has a hint of thyme. Somebody's garden says bonjour.
Lovely to see you out, monsieur! The bench suits you!
A kitchen window, a clatter of pans, a laugh. Good street.

Velvet moss between the steps. Even the steps are cosy.
The swifts are doing loops. Squeaky, happy, very fast.
Fresh-cut grass by the square. Smells like a holiday.
Lovely dog, monsieur! Oh, that is Biscuit. Lovely dog, Biscuit!
The breeze lifts my hair and drops it. Very gentle barber.
Morning sun on my left cheek. Next lap, my right. Fair!
Ting! A spoon on a saucer. The café is officially awake.
Good morning, Inès! You look like a postcard! A fast one!
The hedge by the kiosk is full of bees. Busy, polite bees.
Sand on the promenade. Crunchy shoes. Small beach souvenir.
Merci for the wave, madame! I will wave double next lap!
Smooth old stones by the fountain. Thousands of feet before mine.
Somebody's toast is just right. I can tell by the smell.
Pretty bicycle basket, Lucie! The flowers suit it!
The flag on the kiosk flutters. Flap, flap. Go, go, it says.
Hello, visitor! Lost? Lovely! It is the best way to see it!
The awning cloth snaps in the breeze. Crisp as a fresh shirt.
Morning, Odile! You look very elegant at this hour!
Cool air off the sea on this side. Like opening a fridge. Ah.
A little bell on a shop door just rang. Ding! Somebody's first!
The cobbles go clop under my heels. I am basically a pony.
Warm bread, cold fountain mist, hot cheeks. Three temperatures!
Théo held up his baguette like a torch. Cheering, I think!
Honeysuckle! On the corner! I took a lap's worth of it.
A shutter hook clinked behind me. The house said good morning.
Bonjour, monsieur by the church! You walk with such style!
The palm trunk is rough like a pineapple. I high-fived it.
The fishmonger cart smells of lemons and ice. Fresh!
Leaves skittering along the kerb. They are racing too!
Hello, flowerbed! You smell wonderful after Henri's visit.
Hands on hips. Ears full of cups and gulls and chatter. Lovely.
Catching my breath. The air tastes of salt and something sweet.
That bench is warm already. Thank you, sun. Just one minute.
Have a lovely morning! I am going to be red for an hour!
Leaning on the warm wall. It is like a hug from the town.
Listen! Cups, chimes, cooing. The town is tuning up.
Hello! Sorry, sweaty! Very happy, though! Very happy and sweaty!
The fountain mist on my face. Better than any towel.
Stretching by the hedge. The rosemary is helping, I think.
You look like you slept well! Wonderful! I can tell!
Water from the fountain tap. Cold and sweet. Best drink in town.
Shoes off for a second on the cool tiles. Oh. Bliss.
Phew. Two laps. One sunset. Fair trade.
Made it! The sun waited. Very kind of it.
Hands on the railing. Lungs catching up. View already here.
My mother ran this promenade. I run it slower. On purpose.
Every lap I count the blue shutters. Twelve. Still twelve.
The railing is warm from the whole day. Like a hug.
The clock says half past. My legs say much later.
Lap two, the café awning winked at me. Stripes do that.
Grandpa calls this the good tired. He is right.
Sorry, out of breath. Not out of happy.
I run for the view. The running is just the ticket.
The fountain splashed me on the corner. Thank you, fountain.
Pink sky, orange sky, my face. All matching.
Henri waved his hat. I waved my whole arm. Too much? No.
Shoes off soon. Feet up soon. Sky now.
The kiosk smells of lemon. I nearly stopped. Nearly.
My little sister calls this my sunset spot. It is.
Lap one: fast. Lap two: scenic. Both: lovely.
The string lights just came on. Perfect timing, lights.
Is it a jog if I stop to smell the jasmine? I say yes.
I lean, I puff, I glow. That is the routine.
The roof tiles go copper at this hour. Every one of them.
Dad taught me to finish facing the sun. So I do.
Pace: gentle. Mood: excellent. Shoelaces: holding.
Just catching my breath. And the whole horizon.
Marcel cheered from the door. I ran a little taller.
The gulls are going home too. We have the same schedule.
I said bonjour to the zinc roofs. They shone back.
Someone painted the bench green again. It looks new and proud.
I run past the church clock twice. It always looks pleased.
Breathing like a teapot. A happy teapot.
The cypresses look like they are lining up for the sunset.
Golden legs, golden sky, golden railing. Golden me.
Ran past the palm tree. It gave me a little wave.
This is my favourite minute of the day. Maybe two minutes.
Lap two, a cat watched me from a window box. Very approving.
The sea is doing that glitter thing. My favourite thing.
Someone left their shutters half open. A sleepy house.
Huff, huff, ah. That last ah is the best part.
The awning at the café rolls up at sunset. Bedtime, awning.
Every evening I think I will run three laps. I never do.
The railing has a little dent right here. My dent now.
The lamps along the promenade blink on one by one. Like a cheer.
Dad and I used to race to this rail. He always let me win.
I nodded to the dog. The dog nodded back. Deal made.
Still puffing. Still smiling. Nobody can stop the smiling.
Lavender by the kiosk. I ran through it twice on purpose.
The sun is almost touching the water. Go on, sun.
Personal best tonight: most sunsets admired in one lap.
Legs say rest. Eyes say look. Everyone gets what they want.
The fountain sings a different note at sunset. Lower. Cosier.
Lap two I found a perfect pebble. It is in my pocket now.
The horizon moves a little each night. I come to check.
Window boxes full of geraniums. Red, red, red. Very cheering.
There it goes. Slowly. Like me on lap two.
I counted the steps up to the church once. I lost count. Twice.
This railing has heard a lot of happy sighs. Here is mine.
The shutters on the yellow house are the same blue as the sea.
I always run the last bit on tiptoe. For the drama.
My running shoes are old friends. Tonight they did beautifully.
The sky did purple. I did not know it could do purple.
Hello, café! Hello, kiosk! Goodbye, lap two!
I come every evening. The view never repeats itself.
Some run for medals. I run for this exact colour of pink.
One deep breath of sea air. Then another. Then supper.
The tiles on the promenade go warm and rosy. Lovely to run on.
My brother says I jog like a happy duck. Quack, thank you.
Lap one, I saw the first star. Lap two, it brought a friend.
Hands on knees for a second. Then hands on railing. Better.
The church clock chimed as I finished. A little fanfare.
Sunset, then soup, then sleep. The three S's.
I passed Théo with a baguette. He saluted me with it.
The breeze is cooling my ears. Very thoughtful breeze.
Dad always says: well run, now well watched.
Someone is playing piano behind a shutter. Perfect cool-down.
The clouds look like they ran here too. All stretched out.
I like the bit where the path curves by the fountain. Wheee.
Shoulders down. Breath slow. Sun slower.
The water is copying the sky. Very good copy.
The string lights sway when I run under them. Like a high five.
Sweaty, sandy, smiley. A good evening's work.
Lap two I waved at a window. A grandmother waved back.
Tomorrow, same rail, same time. It is a date, sunset.
My nieces think I run to the end of the world. It is this rail.
The sun dips. My breath steadies. We land together.
The fountain coin is still there. Someone wished well.
If you need me, I will be right here. Glowing.
The palms rustle like applause. I take a little bow.
Just long enough to watch it go. Then a slow walk home.

exchanges: Lucie! I saw a purple wall of bougainvillea!
Obviously. It is the best wall in town.
Inès! You lapped me. Twice. Gorgeously.
Three times. But who is counting? Me.
Henri! Your lemon tree looks lovely tonight!
It was watered twice today. It feels very loved.
Evening, Odile! The jasmine is out!
I know, darling! Henri stopped to sniff it four times!
Biscuit says hello. Biscuit also says walk faster.
Camille, which flowers are those on your balcony?
Geraniums. Léo waters them. Very generously.
Théo! Tomorrow, three laps. Join me?
Tomorrow I am doing nothing. Professionally.
Marcel! Save me a lemonade for tomorrow?
Bravo! One lemonade, reserved for the champion.
Good evening! Lovely roses by the church today.
They are. I count them on my way home. Slowly.
Asgeir! Evening run done. And you?
Bench reached. Same view, less puffing.
Inès! Did you see the bougainvillea? Pinker today!
Saw it lap one. Pinkness: nine out of ten.
Morning, Inès! I am stopping to smell the jasmine!
Inès, how many lemons on the corner tree?
My grandmother ran this road too, Inès!
Then you have her legs. Good legs!
Inès, slow down! The roses want to say hi!
Hi, roses! Bye, roses! See you lap two!
Inès, the sun just hit the zinc roofs!
Six fifty-one. Right on time. Lovely.
Tomorrow I am bringing my little sister, Inès!
Wonderful! I will run very slowly. Promise.
Inès! The post office light is still on!
Open all night. Like me, almost.
Inès, I saw Asgeir wave from his window!
He waves every lap. I count those too.
Inès! I tapped the fountain rim! Lucky lap!
Rim tapped. Logged. Lap count: two.

Gérard, always. He is very punctual.
Inès, I forgot to start my stopwatch again!
I timed you. Lovely pace. Very lovely.
Race you to the café, Inès! Slowly!
Deal. Slowest winner gets the sunny chair.
Inès, my new shoes squeak! Hear them?
Squeak, squeak. Like applause. Keep going!
Inès, how do you never get puffed?
I do. I just puff in rhythm. Puff, puff.
Inès, I am doing my finish-line pose!
Beautiful! Ten out of ten for style!
Inès! The workshop light is on already!
Someone is building things early. Like us!
Inès! Wait! No, go, I will catch up... tomorrow!
Lap nine for me! You are doing great, keep going!
Bonsoir. It is lovelier when one is sitting on it.
Odile! Your scarf matches the sunset!
And your cheeks match it too, darling! Bravo!
Marcel! Save me a table! Second lap!
A table with a view and a very tall water, voilà!
He says hello. He also says you missed a spot.
(Biscuit considers it. Biscuit sits down instead.)
Lucie! Is that a peach in your basket?
Two peaches, obviously. One is for after your lap!
Léo! Want to count my steps?
Okay! One... two... you are going too fast!
Same bench, same sunset. You keep running, I keep sitting.
Asgeir! Coming to the railing for sunset?
Wouldn't miss it. Save me a spot, I'm slower.
Marcel! What smells so good in there?
Bouillabaisse! A bowl waits for you after the lap.
Henri! Are you watering the basil again?
Every evening. It smells better for runners, you know.
Odile! Is that madeleines in your bag?
A dozen, from the bakery. One is yours after the lap!
Lucie! I heard your bike bell from the fountain!
Ding ding! That was for you. Keep going!
Camille! Your kitchen window smells of thyme!

Théo! Is that the evening baguette?
Second one. The first did not survive the walk home.
A cherry ice! It is dripping. I am fine though!
Yusuf! Biscuit's tags jingle like music!
He jingles on purpose. He loves an audience.
Bonsoir! Did you try the socca at the café?
Twice! I am up from the old town just for it.
Asgeir! Is that a lemonade from the kiosk?
Fresh squeezed. I'll have one ready at the railing.
Inès! How many laps for you?
Four. Three left. Go go go!

Like a little swallow, darling. Pink in the cheeks.

Save me a chair, Marcel! After lap two!
Bravo! The sunny one, with a pancake on it.

Camille! You smell of orange blossom!

Théo! Is that a work call?
Yes. Very serious. About croissants. Mostly.
Oh, how kind! I was hoping to find it by accident!
It has me, I think. Every morning. Run well.
Half a lap ahead. As always! Wait, Léo!
Jasmine, young one. Forty years on that gate.
Of course! Run faster, and it is yours. Allez!
Hei. Checking on the post office. It never sleeps.
Mm. After the post. Then a few more screws.
By one lap and two minutes. Not that I counted.

For your legs, yes. Sit when you are ready.

Can I say hello to Biscuit?

Good boy! Do you run too?

Two laps done, Théo! Feel my heartbeat!
I will take your word. I am professionally resting.
Marcel! Water, please. A big one!
Water for the champion! With a lemon, bravo!

All of them are. This one has me on it.
Asgeir! Do you ever run the promenade?
I walk it. Very fast walking, though.
